title: Pair encoding preserves polynomial time
statement: Let $f,g$ be polynomial-time computable functions from bit strings to bit strings. Then the function mapping $x$ to the pair encoding of $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ is polynomial-time computable, where the pair encoding doubles each bit of its first component, appends the separator $01$, and then appends its second component.
replaced: Let $f$ and $g$ be polynomial-time computable functions on bit strings (each computed by some finite binary Turing machine within $C(n+1)^c$ steps on inputs of length $n$, for some constants $C, c$). Then the map $x \mapsto \langle f(x), g(x)\rangle$ is polynomial-time computable, where $\langle a,b\rangle$ denotes the self-delimiting pair encoding of bit strings $a$ and $b$ (every bit of $a$ doubled, then $01$, then $b$).
